Guizhou Tourism Development Commission.desc: A tourism department of the Guizhou provincial government in south-west China, at full provincial-department rank (系正厅级建制). The provincial finance department's 2018 budget disclosure for it sets out ten numbered headings of responsibility, among them carrying out national tourism policy, law and standards, drafting and implementing the province's tourism development plans, provincial tourism resource surveys and tourism statistics, handling travel-agency establishment approvals, supervising tourism market order and quality and coordinating tourism safety, and promoting the province's overall tourism image outside it. It had nine internal departments, and its 2018 budget covered two budget units, the Commission itself and the self-funded Guizhou Provincial Tourism School; the provincial tourism quality supervision office, the provincial tourism information centre and the international mountain tourism development centre are not separately accounted for and sit inside the Commission's own budget.

Rail Assets Holding Company (RAHCO).desc: A Tanzanian state-owned company incorporated by the Railways Act 2002, which names it Reli Assets Holding Company Limited (the project's resettlement-plan amendment and this key use 'Rail'), and whose whole issued share capital was held by the Treasury Registrar. Its objects were to acquire the rail transport functions of the Tanzania Railways Corporation together with transferred property, rights and liabilities, to secure or provide rail infrastructure, and to develop, promote and manage rail infrastructure assets on behalf of the government; it held the Railway Infrastructure Fund on irrevocable trust and could delegate its powers, which the Act says should take the form of concessions where practicable. Under the Act a railway strip 15 metres wide in urban areas and 30 metres in rural areas either side of the track centre line was reserved for future rail development, and building in it needed the company's written permission. The Act was repealed on 28 February 2018 by the Railways Act 2017, which establishes the Tanzania Railways Corporation.

Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo).desc: Ghana's electricity transmission utility and system operator, in its own report's words, incorporated in December 2006 and operational from August 2008, with the Government of Ghana as sole shareholder represented by the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Energy. It transmitted 23,551 GWh in 2023 against a peak demand of 3,618 MW, and its registered name was changed to 'Ghana Grid Company LTD.' with the Registrar of Companies' approval in August 2023.

Societe Nationale d'electricite du Burki.desc: Burkina Faso's state electricity company, named in its own statutes 'Société Nationale d'Electricité du Burkina', without 'Faso'. It is a société d'Etat with a board of directors, governed by the OHADA uniform act on commercial companies, by law 025/99/AN of 16 November 1999 on companies with public capital and by its statutes. Its share capital of 46 billion FCFA, in 4,600,000 shares of 10,000 FCFA each, fully paid, is assigned entirely to the state of Burkina Faso. Communaute Electrique du Benin (CEB).desc: An international public body (organisme international à caractère public) of Benin and Togo, constituted by the two states under the Benin-Togo electricity code annexed to an international agreement between their governments, with its seat in Lomé, Togo. Its capital is divided in equal shares between the two states; the code's text leaves the amount blank. Under article L5 of the code it holds exclusively, across both territories, the activities of transport, importation and single buyer for the two states' needs, may delegate its transport right locally and for a set period to a transporteur délégué, and is the sole supplier of electricity to the distribution networks.

Agence Beninoise d'Electrification Rural.desc: A Beninese public establishment with a non-profit purpose, holding legal personality and organisational and financial autonomy, seated in Cotonou and placed under the supervision of the ministry responsible for energy. Its mission is to support the state's policy on energy efficiency and rural electrification: drawing up national and regional development programmes and running pilot demonstration projects; following energy audits and accrediting the experts who carry them out, and attesting the energy efficiency of equipment; helping set technical standards and specifications for rural electrification installations; drawing up tender files for rural generation or distribution concessions; and mobilising and managing the Rural Electrification and Energy Efficiency Funds. A 2018 decree on off-grid electrification makes it the conceding authority (autorité concédante) for off-grid public electricity service and the body that issues authorisations for systems of 500 kVA or less, once the electricity regulator has approved them.

Multan Electric Power Company (MEPCO).desc: A Pakistani state-owned electricity distribution and supply company, incorporated on 14 May 1998 as a public limited company under the government's policy of unbundling and corporatising the power sector, taking over the assets, rights, obligations and liabilities of the defunct Multan Area Electricity Board together with the grid stations and transmission lines that supplied that area; it is registered under the Companies Act 2017, and the shares are held by the Ministry of Energy (Power Division). It supplies 15 administrative districts of southern Punjab — Multan, Muzaffargarh, Kot Addu, Layyah, D.G. Khan, Taunsa, Rajanpur, Lodhran, Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Khanewal, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Vehari and Bahawalnagar — across 105,505 square kilometres, and in financial year 2024-25 reported 8,816,400 consumers at 30 June 2025, 16,569 million kWh sold, 13,705 employees and Rs 524,062 million from the sale of electricity.

Hyderabad Electric Supply Company (HESCO.desc: Two Pakistani state-owned electricity companies. HESCO was incorporated under section 32 of the Companies Ordinance 1984 on 23 April 1998, registration number L09496 of 1997-98, with its registered office in the WAPDA offices complex at Hussainabad, Hyderabad, Sindh, to take over the assets, functions and responsibilities of WAPDA's then Hyderabad Area Electricity Board; it supplies electricity to consumers in Hyderabad, Tando Allah Yar, Tando Mohammad Khan, Badin, Sujawal, Thatta, Jamshoro, Matiari, Shaheed Benazirabad (Nawabshah), Sanghar, Mirpur Khas, Umerkot and Tharparkar, and its licence of 27 December 2023 makes it supplier of last resort in that territory for 20 years from 27 April 2023 to 26 April 2043. Against a target of 18.63 per cent, its transmission and distribution losses were 27.49 per cent in financial year 2022-23. NTDC, at WAPDA House, Lahore, is in the regulator's words 'a wholly public sector entity' and holds transmission licence TL/01/2002, effective for 30 years from its issue on 31 December 2002, with the exclusive right as grid company in the service territory in its Schedule-I, for which the minimum transmission voltage is declared to be 220 kV and above; a modification approved on 21 March 2023 excludes system-operator functions from that licence, to be licensed separately under section 23G, and requires the functions to be separated within two years of the system operator licence taking effect.

Kampala City Council, later the Kampala.desc: The city government of Kampala, Uganda. The Kampala Capital City Act, assented to on 28 December 2010, published in Uganda Gazette 2 on 14 January 2011 and commenced on 1 March 2011 by the Kampala Capital City (Commencement) Instrument 2011, provides in section 5(1) for an Authority known as the Kampala Capital City Authority, a body corporate which section 5(3) makes the governing body of the Capital City, administering it on behalf of the central government, and provides in section 4(2) that any entity which immediately before the commencement existed as a local government in the delineated area ceases to be a local government. Its chief executive is an executive director appointed by the President on the advice of the Public Service Commission (section 17), and under section 79 the minister responsible for the capital city may vary or rescind, with Cabinet's approval, any decision of the Authority that contravenes any law or Government policy, and has general powers to give directives on policy and general development which the Authority must comply with.

sources.publisher: ULII (Uganda Legal Information Institute)

Kampala City Council, later the Kampala.why: Checked against the statute, and the writer's open question is now closed. CORRECTED: 'may veto decisions that appear illegal' is replaced by what section 79 says — 79(1)(a) is a power 'to vary or rescind any decision of the Authority which is in contravention of any law or Government policy, with the approval of Cabinet', so the writer's version dropped Government policy and the Cabinet condition, and 'veto' is the long title's word rather than the section's. RESOLVED: the Kampala Capital City (Amendment) Act 2022, which the writer flagged as unopened, was opened. Its arrangement of sections has two items, commencement and 'Amendment of section 77 of Act 1 of 2011', and it amends section 77 alone, to let the Minister responsible for the Capital City determine the remuneration of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Council and of division urban council speakers, deemed in force from 1 February 2020. It leaves sections 4, 5, 17 and 79 as the version read prints them, so the hedge that nothing here is current law is withdrawn. The front matter also notes the Act was revised and consolidated as at 31 December 2023 by Uganda's Law Reform Commission, which is where Chapter 195 comes from. The writer's restraint on the card's 'the elected City Council was replaced' stands: section 4(2) strips local-government status without naming the Kampala City Council.

Electricity Distribution and Supply Auth.desc: Sierra Leone's electricity distribution body, established as a body corporate by section 25 of the National Electricity Act 2011 (Act 16 of 2011), which split the former National Power Authority between it and a new Sierra Leone Electricity Generation and Transmission Company and repealed the National Power Authority Act 1982. Under section 34 of the Act, as replaced by the National Electricity (Amendment) Act 2018, it is responsible for the supply, distribution and retail sale of electricity for the entire country except in areas where the regulator has issued a distribution licence to another qualified entity, for dispatch and system control within its territory, for establishing uniform standard voltages as far as practicable and securing supply at reasonable prices; it must buy its electricity from the Company and independent power producers under a power purchase agreement approved by the regulator, and must supply any person requiring supply under a contract on terms it determines. Its board appoints a Director-General as its chief executive, and the Minister responsible for electricity may give it general directions on matters of policy. A 2022 World Bank project document says it owns and operates the main grid and the isolated grids.

Electricity Distribution and Supply Auth.why: REBUILT from the statute, which is the recovery this round was asked to attempt. The writer recorded the statute route as closed because every copy search returns sits on parliament.gov.sl, which refuses fetches as robots_disallowed, and old.sierralii.org carries metadata only. The Act is also mirrored on The Sierra Leone Web, sierra-leone.org/Laws/2011-16.pdf, together with the 2018 amendment at sierra-leone.org/Laws/2018-03.pdf. Both are scans in a shifted-glyph font that extracts as nonsense and had to be rasterised and read by OCR. From them: s.25(1) 'There is hereby established a body to be known as the Electricity Distribution and Supply Authority', s.25(2) body corporate; s.2 establishes the Sierra Leone Electricity Generation and Transmission Company, whose functions include to 'own and operate the existing generating assets of the National Power Authority'; s.34(a)-(g) the functions, with the nationwide responsibility 'except in areas in which the Commission has issued a distribution licence to another appropriately qualified entity' and the dispatch and system-control role; s.35 the power purchase agreement; s.36(1) the duty to supply; s.38 'The Minister may give general directions to the Authority on matters of policy'; s.39(1) the Director-General appointed by the Board; s.77 transferring National Power Authority employees to the Company or the Authority on commencement; and s.82(1) 'The National Power Authority Act 1982 is hereby repealed'. The 2018 Amendment Act repeals and replaces s.34, keeping (a) and the dispatch role and adding a collection-account instrument and third-party agreements. The restatement problem the writer flagged is therefore gone: the entry now rests on statutory content independent of the name. The World Bank project document is kept as the only source for 'owns and operates the main grid and the isolated grids' — which it does state, in section 1.3, 'connected to and served by the main grid and isolated grids EDSA owns and operates' — and is attributed to it, because it is a development-bank document and secondary about the institutions it names, and the Act does not say EDSA owns the grids. Note for the record: the Act's printed body numbers the transfer and repeal sections 77 and 82 while its own arrangement of sections numbers them 76 and 81, and the 2018 amendment's marginal notes call the parent 'Act No. 8 of 2011' where its own cover reads No. 16.

Centre for Accountability and Rule of La.desc: A Freetown-based Sierra Leonean civil society organisation, given its fuller name as the Centre for Accountability and Rule of Law in Sierra Leone (CARL-SL), which is described as committed to promoting human rights through accountability. South African National Parks.desc: South Africa's national parks agency. It was initially established in terms of the now repealed National Parks Act 57 of 1976 and continues to exist in terms of the National Environmental Management: Protected Areas Act 57 of 2003; it is a public entity governed by the Public Finance Management Act 1 of 1999, listed as a Schedule 3 Part A public entity, and submits its five-year strategic plan for approval to the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment as its executive authority. Its mandate is to conserve, protect, control and manage national parks and other defined protected areas and their biological diversity, and it says it manages a system of 21 national parks, including three world heritage sites and ten marine protected areas, comprising over four million hectares on land and almost 370,000 hectares at sea, about 70 per cent of state-owned terrestrial protected areas, with five parks integral components of transfrontier conservation areas with Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and Lesotho.
